findings.title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without required UserModel argument
findings.body: In UsernameForm.authenticate, the new condition `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is invoked with no arguments. The only matching definition in the codebase is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm, which requires a UserModel. As written, this file will fail to compile and the intended re-authentication change will not take effect at all. The call needs to be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, or a no-arg overload must be added (e.g., `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` that delegates to the user-taking version using the current AuthenticationFlowContext).

findings.title: Regression: webauthn conditional UI no longer initialized on the initial login page (user == null)
findings.body: The diff removes `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` from the user==null branch and replaces it with a new check `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))`. Because `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` short-circuits to false when the user argument is null, fillContextForm is now never invoked on a user's first visit to the username+password form. This means the CHALLENGE/RP_ID/conditional-UI attributes are never set on the initial login page, breaking discoverable-credential auto-login and the conditional webauthn button on first paint. The same swap is repeated in `challenge(context, error, field)`, so the conditional UI also disappears from initial-login error pages (invalid username/password). Existing tests `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` in all three test classes plus the first-page assertions of `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`, `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication`, and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` rely on `//form[@id='webauth']` being present and `getUsernameAutocomplete() == "username webauthn"` after `oauth.openLoginForm()`; those assertions will fail. The fix is to call fillContextForm for the initial-login case as well (e.g., drop the `user != null` part of `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` for this caller, or invoke fillContextForm separately whenever `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` regardless of whether the user is set).
